why: Quote is VERBATIM: corporate-launcher.md line 11, fetched with curl -sL, read whole (single sentence, no second-half reversal). The identifier half of the finding is also correct: `grep -ranF` for CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER / processWrapper / PROCESS_WRAPPER / SHELL_PREFIX / shellPrefix over packages+apps (*.ts, *.tsx, *.json) returns 0 hits, and MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501 is exactly the cited array with no launcher key (though it holds 32 keys, not the 34 claimed; the only `execWrapper` in the tree, claude-bash-rule.ts:227/324/337/381, is an unrelated bash-permission-rule parser flag for xargs/find -exec). The finding is refuted on its EVIDENCE ANCHOR and its CONSEQUENCE, which are the two halves this repo's trap list says keep being wrong. (1) The cited line is a DIFFERENT SUBSYSTEM. packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts:238 sits inside `runDependencyInstallerWithQuota`, and `invocation` there comes from `buildPluginRuntimeDependencyInstallInvocation(bunPath, directory, hostEnvironment, frozenLockfile)` (:44-89, command = bunPath, args = bun install flags with a sandboxed HOME/TMPDIR/cache). It spawns the PLUGIN RUNTIME DEPENDENCY INSTALLER under a quota watchdog. It has nothing to do with stdio MCP servers; the finding named the wrong subsystem. (2) 'Subprocesses are spawned directly ... spawns stdio MCP servers' is FALSE. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:724, in SupervisedStdioClientTransport.startProcess, starts every stdio MCP server through `this.authority.processSupervisor.start({ ... semanticId: 'plugin-mcp-stdio' ... })`, and ProcessSupervisor spawns the ISOLATION-REWRITTEN argv `plan?.command ?? request.command` / `plan?.args ?? args` at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:244, behind a `beforeStart` admission gate. A launcher-prefix chokepoint therefore exists and is live: packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/trusted-isolation-launchers.ts:23 `resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher` resolves absolute host-owned launcher paths (sandbox-exec/bwrap/firejail/unshare) from a fixed allowlist that deliberately never consults PATH, and filesystem-/network-isolation build the prefixed argv the supervisor then spawns. (3) Even had stdio MCP been spawned raw, it would be evidence for a DIFFERENT page. The same doc, line 137 (section 'Relationship to CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX'), states that CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER wraps Claude Code's own processes while CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX wraps 'the shell commands Claude runs on your behalf, such as Bash tool calls, hooks, and the commands that start stdio MCP servers', and that 'a launcher written for one doesn't work as the other'. The finding's sole spawn-site anchor is out of this page's scope by the page's own text. (4) The doc's covered process classes have largely no analogue here. Lines 23-30 scope the launcher to the on-demand background service, agent-view terminal hosts and warm-standby sessions, post-update self-relaunches, Remote Control workers, and tmux/iTerm2 teammate panes - the CLI's supervisor architecture. Nessy Desktop is an Electron app with none of it: the post-update restart is electron-updater's `quitAndInstall` (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts:14, 'quitAndInstall() handles restart natively - no external scripts'), performed by the OS installer rather than a self-spawn from our own binary; subagents and workflows are IN-PROCESS child sessions via `spawnChildSession` (orchestrator/spawner.ts, called at subtask.ts:95, workflow-tool.ts:358 and :390, review-tool.ts:309, guardian-runner.ts:71), so there is no OS process to prefix. The one genuinely unwrapped self-spawn is the headless server at apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:63 (`Bun.spawn(['bun','run',serverEntry])`), and even that resolves its entry by walking the MONOREPO layout to packages/server/src/index.ts, i.e. the dev/CLI harness path, not a packaged-binary self-spawn. (5) It is not an undiscovered gap. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (read all nine: seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries), but it IS a dated recorded scoping note: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:715 files it as 'Adjacent and worth a decision, not necessarily a build', and :727 records the reason - 'The corporate-launcher half is the weakest part for us, since it is written against the CLI's own supervisor architecture, which we do not have.' The finding's ourState cites :725 while missing both :715 and :727, i.e. it cites the fact-capture line and omits the two lines that already scoped it. Severity is further inflated by omitting the page's own limits: the mechanism is ignored entirely on Windows (line 32, 'the launcher contract depends on exec') and requires v2.1.208 / v2.1.210 (line 16).
correctedState: No admin-facing corporate-launcher CONFIGURATION exists - no reader for CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER, `processWrapper`, CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX or any NESSY_-prefixed analogue (grep -ranF over packages+apps, 0 hits), and MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (managed-policy.ts:501-534, 32 keys) carries no launcher key. What is missing is the configuration surface, NOT the mechanism: a host-owned launcher-prefix path already exists and is live for supervised children - resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher (packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/trusted-isolation-launchers.ts:23) resolves sandbox-exec/bwrap/firejail/unshare from a fixed allowlist that never consults PATH, and ProcessSupervisor spawns the rewritten `plan?.command ?? request.command` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:244) behind a beforeStart gate. Stdio MCP servers route through that chokepoint (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:724, semanticId 'plugin-mcp-stdio') and are NOT spawned directly; per the page's own line 137 they would in any case belong to CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX, not to this page. The cited anchor packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts:238 is the plugin runtime DEPENDENCY INSTALLER (`bun install` under a quota watchdog, invocation built at :44-89), not an MCP spawn. Of the page's covered classes, the background service, agent-view hosts/warm spares, Remote Control workers and tmux teammate panes have no analogue in an Electron desktop app; the post-update relaunch is electron-updater's quitAndInstall (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts), performed by the OS installer; subagents and workflows are in-process child sessions. The only genuinely unwrapped self-spawn is the headless server at apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:63, on the monorepo dev path. Scope was already recorded 2026-07-26 at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:715 ('worth a decision, not necessarily a build') with the reason at :727 ('written against the CLI's own supervisor architecture, which we do not have'). The decision is owed, not taken - this is a scoping question, not a defect.
